title: Compare with the Next Row Using LEAD
learning_objective: Learn how to compare each log row with the row immediately after it.

tutorial.explanation: LEAD is the opposite of LAG. It reads from a later row in the ordered result, which helps detect whether the current value continues into the next row.
tutorial.syntax: SELECT id, num, LEAD(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_num FROM logs;
tutorial.mental_model: LAG looks backward. LEAD looks forward. Together, they let one row inspect both neighbors.

guided_example.prompt: Show each log row with the next num value.
guided_example.solution_query: SELECT id, num, LEAD(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_num FROM logs ORDER BY id;
guided_example.explanation: Each row sees the num from the following row. The last row has no next value, so next_num is NULL.

practice.prompt: Return rows where num is the same as the next row's num.
practice.expected_query: WITH compared AS (SELECT id, num, LEAD(num) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_num FROM logs) SELECT id, num FROM compared WHERE num = next_num ORDER BY id;

hints: Rows at the end of a sequence may have next_num as NULL.
Filter after calculating the window value.
